case_title: State of N.C.T. of Delhi v. Ajay Kumar Tyagi
statutory_provisions: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 s.7, s.13
evidence_type: Trap-based complaint by the complainant constable (as alleged by the prosecution); the Supreme Court did not assess evidence on merits
trial_court_outcome: Not stated (charges framed by the Special Judge; no verdict or sentence in the judgment)
high_court_outcome: Criminal proceedings quashed under s.482 Cr.P.C. on the ground that the accused was exonerated in the departmental proceedings
neutral_facts: An application for a water connection in the name of a constable's wife was cleared at a lower level and the file was then sent to the accused, a junior engineer in a water board. The complainant, a police constable who was the applicant's husband, lodged a report with the anti-corruption branch alleging that the accused had demanded a bribe of Rs. 2000 to clear the file, with Rs. 1000 to be paid initially and the balance after clearance. A trap was laid. According to the prosecution, the accused demanded and accepted Rs. 1000 as the bribe. This led to registration of a first information report under Sections 7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act. After investigation, a charge-sheet was submitted in September 2002. In parallel, a departmental inquiry was initiated on the same allegation that the accused had demanded, accepted and obtained Rs. 1000 as illegal gratification in consideration of giving a report on the water connection. The inquiry officer recorded that the evidence on record did not substantiate the charge of demand and acceptance of bribe, and found the charge not proved due to lack of evidence on record.
attempt_completion: Completed (as alleged by the prosecution; not decided by the Supreme Court)
number_of_offences: 2 charged (ss.7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Rs. 1000 alleged bribe amount (alleged by prosecution; not decided by the Court)
motive: alleged: monetary gratification (bribe) for clearing the water connection file
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25.8.2008; Supreme Court: 31 August 2012
legal_representation: Accused (respondent): Chelan Sharma, Bake Bihari Sharma (for Asha Gopalan Nair). State (appellant): J.S. Attry, Anjani Aiyagari, Gargi Khanna, B.V. Bairam Das
investigation_status: FIR registered under ss.7/13 PC Act; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed 19 September 2002; charges framed
appeal_history: Trial court: charges framed, outcome not stated. High Court: quashed criminal proceedings on 25.8.2008 under s.482 Cr.P.C. Supreme Court: High Court order set aside and appeal allowed; proceedings restored
prosecution_argument: The High Court's premise of exoneration was unfounded because the inquiry officer's report was not final and was yet to be considered by the disciplinary authority, which could disagree and punish the accused
defence_argument: At such a distance of time the disciplinary authority is precluded from passing any order, so the disciplinary proceeding should be deemed ended in exoneration; the criminal case should be quashed relying on P.S. Rajya
legal_principle_applied: Exoneration in departmental proceedings does not ipso facto quash a criminal prosecution; standard of proof is lower in departmental proceedings; the disciplinary authority is not bound by the inquiry officer's conclusion
precedent_relied_upon: State v. M. Krishna Mohan (2007) 14 SCC 667; Supdt. of Police (C.B.I.) v. Deepak Chowdhary (1995) 6 SCC 225; CBI v. V.K. Bhutiani (2009) 10 SCC 674 (relied on). P.S. Rajya v. State of Bihar (1996) 9 SCC 1 distinguished; State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992 Supp (1) SCC 335) referred to
other_sentence_order: Accused to appear before the trial court within four weeks; trial judge directed to dispose of the criminal case expeditiously and avoid unnecessary adjournments; departmental proceeding to be reopened and kept in abeyance till conclusion of criminal case
